changes: Added the CP-0013 A1 fixed-width code-object transport authority with pointer-free BEGIN/CHUNK/COMMIT records, capability negotiation, manifest validation, and explicit zero-address ACK rules.
Added runtime-owned bounded HSACO staging with per-chunk CRC-32C, whole-image SHA-256, owner/generation/order validation, immutable commit, and deterministic failure cleanup.
Added gem5 protocol, bridge routing, ELF/PT_LOAD and descriptor admission checks, and owner-scoped staging state without mapping or execution.
Retained GCC Debug and Clang ASan/UBSan matrices, native gem5 mold/24 authority builds, independent authority tests, and clean child identity evidence.
limitations: CP-0013 proves A1 transport and daemon-owned staging only. It does not map PT_LOAD ranges, apply relocations, publish kernarg bytes, construct an AQL packet, submit a queue, execute gem5 instructions, or claim GPU visibility, decoder admission, kernel correctness, hardware presence, timing, or performance.
The A1 image is copied into bounded daemon-owned staging and committed by digest; ACK mapping_base_va, descriptor_va, code_va, and kernarg_va remain zero, including on COMMIT success.
The CP-0012 generated vecadd artifact remains an observation and is not an A1 execution fixture. A2 loader/mapping, A3 AQL/kernarg, and A4 queue/decoder execution are separate gates.
Runtime coverage is GCC Debug and Clang ASan/UBSan static matrices; shared-library/package ABI coverage and production ROCr/KFD/HIP/OpenCL compatibility are not claimed.
No Triton, PyTorch, vLLM, model, multi-daemon, collective, or performance claim is made by this checkpoint.
